## p84 A/B — Release of oil and Black Sea shipping safety

**Sources on this page:** p84 A, p84 B.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p84-ab-p84-ab--release-of-oil-and-black-sea-shipping-safety"></a>


[Coordinate certificate](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/certificates.json)

**Two complete, unchanged-source readings.** The published 28–31 October key
deciphers all **223 plaintext positions** from **446 received coordinates**.
Neither record needs a source correction, missing-coordinate fill or new key
assignment. The page is headed **30 October 1918**, while both reception
headers explicitly say **1 November**; these date layers remain distinct.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p84-ab-a-has-the-order-to-release-the-oil-succeeded"></a>

### A: Has the order to release the oil succeeded?

**Readable German:**

> Drahtet, ob erneuter Befehl Izzet Pascha — Izzet Pascha — zur Freigabe
> der Oele Erfolg gehabt hat. Kriegsamt, Kriegsrohstoffabtlg.
> Nr. 0, roem. 1.

**Meaning:** Telegraph whether Izzet Pasha's renewed order to release the
oil has been successful. The signature names the War Office's raw-materials
department. The clear routing names Captain Gerlach at Batum as the
representative of the Prussian War Ministry.

The name **IZZETPASCHA** occurs twice in the decrypted text, separated by
`X`; both occurrences are preserved. Its repetition is not repaired by
deleting ciphertext. The footer is literally **0ROEM1**. Its intended
administrative notation is not independently established.

The [source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p84_A.png) gives
`FUER POT v NKJ (4.17 a.m., November 1st)` and `RICHI-244`. A time before
`(30)` is partly illegible. All 244 ciphertext coordinates are legible.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
DRAHTETOBERNEUTERBEFEHLIZZETPASCHAXIZZETPASCHAZURFREIGABEDEROELEERFOLGGEHABTHATXXKRIEGSAMTKRIEGSROHSTOFFABTLGXNRX0ROEMX1XX
```

</details>

All **122/122** positions follow directly from the stated source and key.
The displayed prose adds spacing and punctuation only.

The [p83 A source edition](083.md#edition-cases-naval-gerlach-oil-release-query) preserves the same
244-coordinate body. Its clearer internal heading reads `1830 (30)`; the
partly illegible p84 time remains transcribed as such. The p83 edition also
retains a conservative five-overprint mask branch, for which the clear p84
coordinates supply the five fills.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p84-ab-b-request-daily-reports-on-black-sea-shipping"></a>

### B: Request daily reports on Black Sea shipping

**Readable German:**

> Erbitten fuer Truppenkdo. Kaukasus, wenn moeglich taeglich, kurze
> Mitteilung, ob Schwarze-Meerschiffahrt gefaehrdet.

**Meaning:** The Caucasus troop command requests a short daily report,
if possible, on whether shipping in the Black Sea is at risk. The message
asks for the assessment; it does not itself report that shipping is unsafe.

The [source](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/sources/p84_B.png) gives
`OSM v NKJ (3.30 a.m., November 1st)`, the clear routing
`316 15/10 V POT 1021 FUER OSM UND COS (30) VON POT`, and `RICHI-202`.
The body has exactly 202 valid coordinates.

**Raw output:**


</details>

All **101/101** positions are fixed with no source edit.

<a id="edition-cases-naval-p84-ab-source-verification-and-credit"></a>

### Source, verification and credit

J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*, printed
p84 / PDF page 87 in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source package](../../experiments/corpus_recovery/README.md) retains
every literal coordinate, source-image hash and plaintext-coordinate pair.
Both plaintexts independently re-encrypt to the complete, unchanged source.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

The published period key keeps the historical and modern researchers'
attribution in [the key register](../../data/keys.json). Source inspection,
exact verification and this edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

## p84 C — Field post, illness and a conditional request to come

**Edition context:** p84 C — Illness and a request to come.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p84-mother-illness-extension-p84-c--illness-and-a-request-to-come"></a>


[Evidence and verifier](../../experiments/p84_mother_illness_fragment/README.md)
· [Earlier field-post fragment](../../experiments/p84_field_post_fragment/README.md)

**Recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
An additional conditional clause fits the interrupted p84 C reception:
**Mutter schwer krank. Bitte komm.** The combined conditional proposals assign **52/122
positions**, including the previously proposed *Deutsche Feldpost*, while
retaining every observed coordinate. The unchanged key and raw source frame
still fix **14/122** positions. Seventy positions remain unassigned under these proposals.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p84-mother-illness-extension-conditional-reading"></a>

### Conditional reading

**Readable German — conditional lexical proposal; the surrounding passages remain unresolved:**

> […] Deutsche Feldpost […] [Mutter schwer krank. Bitte komm.] […]

**Meaning under this proposal:** A mother is seriously ill, and the recipient
is asked to come. The field-post fragment supplies a plausible setting for a
personal telegram. The relationship, destination and identities are not
established by the surviving text.

**Readable German — an equally compatible lexical counterexample:**

> […] Deutsche Feldpost […] [Mittelschwer krank. Bitte komm.] […]

This alternative means approximately “moderately ill; please come.” It changes
`MUTTER` to `MITTEL`, while retaining exactly the same coordinate prices in all
five frames. At position **69**, `U` and `I` share the observed half-coordinate;
position **73**, proposed as `R` or `L`, is wholly absent. The family-message
interpretation is a contextual preference, not a unique recovery of `MUTTER`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p84-mother-illness-extension-source-and-retained-frames"></a>

### Source and retained frames

Childs, printed p84 / PDF page 87, labels the reception
`C) FUER COS (4.30 a.m., November 1st)` and `1810 (30); RICHI-244`.
The page heading is 30 October. The source ends with **Balance jammed**.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 118 printed slots; seven dash masks and the short FDFG group retained:**

```text
AFDAX AXGFD GXAVV AXDVG DAADV VXAGX GDVAA AXGGX
AAAXA FXDDG DXXGX DFDVF FAXXX FXGGA AXGFG FDFG
DADDA AVAFV XGXAD AAAAX DVXAF XAXXG FA--- ----
```

</details>

As in the earlier edition, one unobserved slot is inserted inside or beside
the four-character `FDFG` group, before source index **75, 76, 77, 78 or 79**.
Another 125 unobserved slots supply the interrupted tail and reach the
advertised 244. All 111 observed symbols and seven printed masks retain
their source identities and relative order. The published 28–31 October
square and 18-column rank order are unchanged.

The new clause favors three of those existing frames without changing an
observation. The table includes the previous field-post words and the new
clause; it applies equally to the `MUTTER` and `MITTEL` alternatives.

| Insert before source index | Observed substitutions | Printed-mask fills | Added-slot fills | Observed coordinates supporting the new 27-position span |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 75 | 2 | 5 | 43 | 23 |
| 76 | 1 | 5 | 43 | 23 |
| 77 | 0 | 5 | 43 | 23 |
| 78 | 0 | 5 | 42 | 24 |
| 79 | 0 | 5 | 42 | 24 |

Frame **78** is the representative edition. Frame **79** has the same minimum
price; frame **77** also fits without an observed substitution. These are
word-conditioned comparisons. They do not establish the historical loss
position. Frames 75 and 76 remain explicit counterfactual comparisons; their
substitutions are not adopted as source corrections.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p84-mother-illness-extension-raw-and-edited-outputs"></a>

### Raw and edited outputs

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — common to all five frames; 14/122 fixed positions; no fills or observed substitutions:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????D????????E????????7????????S????????N????????M????????N????????E????????G??
```

**Edited output — conditional MUTTER proposal in frame 78; 0 observed substitutions, 5 printed-mask fills and 42 added-slot fills; 52/122 fixed positions:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????DEUTSCHEFELDPOST??7??MUTTERSCHWERKRANKBITTEKOMMX??????N????????E????????G??
```

**Edited output — equally compatible MITTEL counterexample; the same 0 substitutions, 5 printed-mask fills and 42 added-slot fills:**

```text
??9????????G????????U????????E????????R????????DEUTSCHEFELDPOST??7??MITTELSCHWERKRANKBITTEKOMMX??????N????????E????????G??
```

</details>

The new string occupies zero-based positions **68–94**. In frames 78 and 79,
it retains **24 observed supporting coordinates**: `S` at 74, `N` at 83 and
`M` at 92 are already fixed by complete pairs; eighteen further positions
retain one observed half. Six positions are wholly absent and supplied by
the lexical proposal: **T71, R73, K80, A82, E89 and O91**. The counterexample
supplies `L73` instead of `R73`. The final `X94` is a compatible proposed
separator with one observed half.

Compared with the previous 28-position edition, this adds **24 proposed
positions**, costing **three further printed-mask fills and 27 further
added-slot fills** in either minimum-price frame. The `9` and `7` labels in
the surrounding text stay literal and are not expanded into a post-office
number. The text after the proposed separator is unresolved.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p84-mother-illness-extension-discovery-verification-and-limits"></a>

### Discovery, verification and limits

A scan of the unchanged half-coordinate domains located the independent-book
words `MUTTER` or `MITTEL` at 68, `SCHWER` at 74, `KRANK` at 80 and `BITTE`
at 85. Examining the other retained frames then permitted `KOMM` at 90.
All five proposed words and the `MITTEL` counterexample occur in the existing
hash-pinned 53,465-word lexicon built from ten German books. Their composition
into the clause and the preference for a family message are editorial
judgments. No independent native ciphertext donor or authenticated repeat
of this clause has been identified.

The earlier `DEUTSCHEFELDPOST` corpus match, its discovery and its source
controls remain credited in the [previous edition](../../experiments/p84_field_post_fragment/README.md).
Those controls do not validate the newly composed clause. No corrected
statistical significance or exhaustive historical uniqueness is claimed.

The new verifier reconstructs the grid, all five source maps, every marginal
letter domain, both word alternatives and each separate repair ledger. It
checks that the three zero-substitution candidates retain all 111 observations,
then re-encrypts complete witnesses under one unchanged global square.
Arbitrary values in unassigned witness slots are not proposed historical
text. Optional PDF verification authenticates the original scan and the
declared crop pixels; no new image asset is required.

Historical source: **J. Rives Childs**. Published key: **George Lasry, Ingo
Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016)** and **Lasry's 2017 key list**.
Earlier fragment and new lexical extension: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
